critique: The red-coated painter touching up a monumental stack of yellow, blue, and red discs is a witty, boldly scaled Bauhaus conceit, with the narrow central axis and vast navy ground giving the primary geometry real authority. The animated loom, tiny near-invisible guinea pig, and photorealistic paint props introduce three competing ideas; enlarging the animal into a purposeful geometric participant or removing it and letting the painter-and-column gag stand alone would sharpen the functional minimalism.
